proposals.name: Tessera
proposals.concept: Bento header: name, portrait, contact and each key number in separate tiles on a 4-column grid; one body column with section names as label tiles in a left gutter; no side column.
proposals.structureKey: modular bento tile masthead over a gutter-labelled single column

references.title: Banani — Bento grid
references.idea: modules of different sizes on one grid; size = priority

references.title: Framer — Bento CV
references.idea: a personal profile told in tiles (web)

references.title: Contra — Joobin Job Seeker bento design
references.idea: bento tiles for job-seeker data

references.title: Smashing — Lessons from Swiss style
references.idea: one modular grid governing every element

decision.reason: Only the header is new: below the bento tiles the page is the existing label-column body (Press/Column/Ledger) re-decorated with pill labels; the tile header is a common web-portfolio look. Typical CV spills to a ~30%-full page 2 (label gutter wastes width); sparse page is a big empty tile; key-number tiles are mostly empty fill; orbit art barely visible. Reviewer scores avg 7.69 — no credible path to 9.5.

proposals.name: Byline
proposals.concept: Editorial front page: ruled masthead with the name; the person's own profile lifted into a large pull-quote statement beside a captioned portrait + contact column; kicker-ruled sections, hanging-margin dates, narrow list column.
proposals.structureKey: ruled editorial masthead with hoisted pull-quote statement and captioned portrait column

references.title: We and the Color — editorial InDesign CV
references.idea: career as a feature story; serif heads over sans body

references.title: Pepper IT — annual reports that get read
references.idea: by-the-numbers row beside commentary

references.title: Smashing — Lessons from Swiss style
references.idea: rules as structure; asymmetric text block against a narrow column

decision.reason: APPROVE: changes content presentation, not decoration — the person's own profile becomes the hero pull-quote under a ruled masthead beside a captioned portrait column; no existing design does this. Suits senior and conservative fields the colour-field graphic designs do not. Initial score 8.25 with fixable polish issues.

blockers: Originality ~8.7: only the header is new; the body (hanging dates, kicker rules, list column) is close to Linea/Folio/Press — needs an editorial body structure of its own (e.g. run-in dates, a caption-style aside continuing the photo-credit idea).
Graphical quality ~8.8: diamond markers and tinted chips are generic against the masthead; replace with small-caps kickers and run-in or ruled skill lists.
Layout ~8.9: on dense and long-profile CVs the header takes 50-60% of page 1 so only one job fits and the main column ends early.
Graphite / no-photo initials block is heavy; short profiles centred leave the PROFILE kicker floating.

CI: removing the rejected bento block shifts the seeded random-spec sequence and contrast.test.ts now hits a pre-existing composer weakness (accent side heading on a soft side fill at 4.43-4.45:1, non-graphic specs). Not caused by Byline, but the branch is not green until it is fixed.

proposals.structureKey: annual report key figures hero with name as running masthead

references.title: Pepper IT — annual reports
references.idea: by-the-numbers spread

decision.reason: Depends on key numbers: sparse and early-career CVs have none, so the hero would be empty or need invented figures (contract forbids). Overlaps the number bands of poster/band designs.

proposals.name: Tabula
proposals.concept: The whole CV is set as ruled information tables, like a timetable or an annual-report schedule: a fact-table header (contact cells and key numbers on one grid), and every section as a table with its own column-header row, a fixed key column (dates, years, skill groups), a content column and a right column for organisation and place; descriptions span the last two columns. Continuation pages carry a running table strip.

references.idea: A strict information grid where every fact has a fixed column

references.title: Tufte: resumes and presentation of data
references.idea: A CV as presentation of data rather than decoration

blockers: Concept: body not structurally new enough (reviewer)
Continuation pages do not repeat section and column heads
Key-number cell proportions; band option orphan stat
implementation.note: Design files not merged; branch scout/2026-11-17 keeps the table building block for reference.

decision.reason: REJECT: the body is a rearranged existing body (Linea/Scholar dates-left entries with the organisation moved right; Ledger numbered heads; inline skill lists as Brief/Clarity) and ruled date|role|company rows are a common template-shop layout; the column-head row is typographic dressing. The header (big name, ruled contact strip, key-number cells) is the Blueprint/Cyber/Ocean family and the rejected swiss-poster. Continued sections do not reopen with their heads; running strip name off the grid and role truncated. Defects: typical CV spills to a ~40% page 2; unequal key-number cells; orphaned inline stat and uneven rules in the band option; email broken mid-word on the extreme CV. Reads as an ATS-family document, themes barely show. Could live as an entry-style option on an existing block, not as a new design.

references.title: Tufte CSS

decision.reason: Moving organisation, place and dates into an outer margin is the same body family as Linea/Scholar (dates in a gutter) and Press/Ledger (label column), mirrored; it would not pass the whole-template rule for the body. Not built so the day is not filled with a weak second design.

proposals.structureKey: impact-first entries with a pulled key figure beside each role

proposals.name: Raster
proposals.concept: The CV set on a visible six-column modular grid (Swiss grid systems, Vignelli's Unigrid). Page 1 opens with a row of two modules: a solid colour module (columns 1-4) carrying the name and role, and a portrait module (columns 5-6) of the same height, with the contact details aligned to the grid beneath. The body is made of modules instead of a stack of entries: each job's achievements are set as tiles two to a row, each tile opened by a short rule; education, projects and similar entries are half-width modules side by side; skill groups, languages and certificates are rows of three modules. Every continuation page opens with the same two-module row in small: a name strip over columns 1-4 and a page-number module over columns 5-6.
proposals.structureKey: two module masthead over a modular grid body with achievement tiles and half width entry modules

references.title: Josef Muller-Brockmann, Grid Systems in Graphic Design (Niggli)
references.idea: A modular grid where every element occupies whole module fields

references.title: Unigrids (Vignelli, US National Park Service)
references.idea: A strong title band and content placed in standard panels of one system

references.title: IxDF: how to use grid systems
references.idea: Modular grid vs column grid: content units snap to modules in both directions

references.title: Navig8: annual report design, the year's highlights
references.idea: Highlights set as a grid of separate tiles rather than a list

proposals.nearestExisting: aurora / coral / electric / magenta / solar (0.788 by the tool); by eye the poster family for the header, Grid/Tiles/Mosaic for the body

decision.reason: APPROVE (conditional): the body is structurally new: a job's points are tiles two to a row, entries are half-width modules, and short sections share a row as modules; no catalogue body or past proposal does this, and it is the gap the 11-16/11-17 learnings name. The continuation pages are new too: a small name strip beside a page module on the grid. The header is the weakest zone (near the poster family) but acceptable. It is sober enough for engineering, operations, healthcare and trades. Risks: the grid idea is under-expressed (the grid is never visible; the only art is the corner square and the same red square on every heading), and there are visible defects: a broken email on the extreme CV, a ~25% page 2 for the typical CV on Letter, blank page feet, and orphan half-width modules.

blockers: Concept ceiling (rounds 3 and 4 reviewers): one top-to-bottom column whose points sit two to a row; header still reads as a dark band plus photo, openers are conventional; originality and visual sophistication top out about 8.5-8.8
Points carried to the next page have no job context (no 'continued' marker); the engine only repeats the running header
Blank page feet (about 13-15% on dense and extreme page 1) because tile rows and two-row jobs are kept whole
Uneven tile rows: a short point beside a long one leaves a hole; module rows of unequal length (dense page 3)
Weak header art: faint gutter stubs, flat initials slab without a photo; short profile leaves columns 5-6 empty, long profile in two columns breaks mid-sentence
implementation.note: Converged at 8.5-8.7 over four rounds; the fifth round was not spent. PR #6 stays open as a draft and must not be merged. It also holds a real engine fix: the generated design index now imports JSON with { type: 'json' }, without which the first design file on main breaks the Playwright e2e step.

proposals.concept: Section heads as signage panels with pictograms and arrows.
proposals.structureKey: signage panel section heads with pictograms over a single column

learnings: 2026-11-16: a new header over an existing body column is not a new structure (Tessera rejected: bento tiles over the label-column body). The reviewer judges the whole page, not the masthead.

2026-11-16: changing content presentation (the person's own profile lifted into a hero pull-quote) is what got approved; but four review rounds converged on ~9.0 because the body stayed conventional. Next time design the body structure with the same care as the header before building.

2026-11-16: gaps still open — no design yet with an editorial/structural body of its own among graphic designs; professions still thin: healthcare, trades and academic-graphic. Engine traps found: the Tailwind Prettier plugin strips leading spaces inside className template literals (use classes()); data-design graphic designs were invisible to Instant Makeover's graphic rule (fixed in the open PR).

2026-11-16 (owner): uniqueness is judged for the whole template — the body must always be structurally new, plus the header or continuation pages. Header-only ideas (e.g. Byline's statement masthead, Tessera's bento tiles) are kept as header variants for existing building blocks, not proposed as new designs.

2026-11-17: Tabula (everything as ruled tables with When/What/Where heads) was rejected: rows of date | role | organisation are still the dates-left entry with the company moved right. A column-head row and hairlines are dressing, not structure. In this engine the body is a stack of additive blocks per column, so real body novelty has to change what a block shows or how columns relate, not how a stacked entry is ruled.

2026-11-17: before building, check that every claimed zone is actually drawn: the proposal claimed continued sections reopen with their heads, but the paginator only repeats the running header. Also check the typical CV's page fill (a ~40% page 2 is a defect) and the option variants, not only the default.

2026-11-17: gaps still open after two runs: a graphic body that is structurally new (not gutter/label/timeline/stacked); healthcare, trades and academic. Gloss (per-entry margin notes) was dropped for the same reason as Tabula: meta in a gutter is the Linea/Press family. Engine notes: the stress executive fixture is US Letter by default (set pageSize for A4 PDFs); text in [data-num]/.g-mono is flattened to pictures in the PDF, which is how furniture text stays out of the ATS read; randomGraphic can take a new layout without an extra random draw so other random specs stay unchanged.

2026-11-18: a structurally new body was approved for the first time (Raster: points as tiles two to a row, entries and short sections as modules), but four review rounds converged at 8.5-8.7. Reviewers judged that bullets in two columns still read as a single column, and that a modular body needs the grid to shape the header and openers too, plus points that page-break gracefully. Next: before building, sketch how the idea looks on page 2 of a 3-page CV, not only on page 1.

2026-11-18: engine lessons: (1) text filled in after measuring ([data-num] section numbers) must not change a block's height, or blocks overflow the page foot (give the number and title one line box); (2) a two-column profile below ~300 characters broke the import read-back of short CVs; (3) the first design file on main needs the JSON import attribute in data/index.ts or Playwright e2e fails (fixed in the generator on the Raster PR); (4) bulletRow/entryRow/sectionRow are reusable body capabilities left on the Raster branch.

2026-11-18: gaps still open: a graphic design whose header, openers and body share one expressive structure; healthcare, trades and academic still thin. Recorded variants: wayfinding (heading), spreads (continuation); dropped: lexicon (run-in prose is slow to scan), pillars, lead-story (Byline family), tenure-bars, periodic.
